newsitem.title: USA: ELEK-TEK agrees to recapitalization plan.
newsitem.headline: ELEK-TEK agrees to recapitalization plan.

text.p: ELEK-TEK Inc said Friday it has agreed to a recapitalization plan that would give a Chicago-based investment group voting control of the company.

Bookcase Investment L.L.C. offered to pay $3.00 a share in cash to ELEK-TEK shareholders and invest $10 million to $15 million in a newly issued preferred stock. That would give Bookcase voting control of the company, which would then be privately owned, ELEK-TEK said in a news release.
ELEK-TEK, founded in Chicago in 1979, markets microcomputer products and services through eight retail stores, a national catalog sales operation and a direct sales division.

Bookcase's proposal requires approval by the company's two largest stockholders, Mort Goldman and the estate of Hal Goldman. It also requires renegotiation of certain leases, replacement or renegotiation of credit agreements, regulatory approvals and other conditions.
The proposed transaction also requires approval by ELEK-TEK's directors.
In mid-April, ELEK-TEK hired a financial advisor to explore business options including sale of the company.

In the second half of last year, the company took several steps to improve its profitability. ELEK-TEK had reported a 1996 loss of $10.6 million on sales of $333.5 million. As a result of the loss, the company was in violation of certain requirements of its credit agreements.
Shares of ELEK-TEK were trading up 5/16 to 2-13/16.
